title: Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to Step Down After Decade at Helm
excerpt: Flipkart confirmed the Group CEO's exit on November 25. His last day is reported to be December 4, with a successor to be named in the coming weeks and the IPO still deferred.
body:
• Flipkart Group confirmed on Wednesday, November 25, that Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy will step down and leave the company, ending a run as chief executive that began in January 2017.
  • His last working day will be December 4, according to Walmart International CEO Chris Nicholas, as reported by Bloomberg; a successor will be announced in the coming weeks.
  • Chief product and technology officer Balaji Thiagarajan and the Flipkart board will lead the company in the interim.
  • No official reason was given. The Economic Times reported disagreements with Walmart over the deferred Flipkart IPO and an employee liquidity event, citing people aware of the matter.

Flipkart Group said on Wednesday, November 25, that Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy will step down and leave the company, closing one of the longest chief-executive tenures in Indian e-commerce. The company confirmed the exit in a statement reported by Reuters, hours after Moneycontrol first reported that an emergency town hall had been called amid speculation about his departure.

Krishnamurthy spent more than 11 years at Flipkart across his stints with the company. He became chief executive in January 2017 and Group CEO in 2018, the year Walmart acquired a majority stake in Flipkart for $16 billion. Walmart now holds about 80 per cent of the company, according to The Economic Times, and Flipkart has a registered user base of more than 500 million, according to Reuters.

What happens next

Walmart has begun a search for a successor, and Flipkart said a new chief executive would be announced in the coming weeks. Bloomberg reported, via Mint, that Krishnamurthy's last working day will be December 4, according to Walmart International CEO Chris Nicholas. Until a successor is named, chief product and technology officer Balaji Thiagarajan and the Flipkart board will lead the organisation, the company said. Walmart said it "remains committed" to Flipkart and its long-term opportunity in India.

Reported friction over the IPO

Flipkart gave no official reason for the exit. The Economic Times, citing people aware of the matter, reported that Krishnamurthy met Walmart's leadership in Bentonville, in the United States, earlier in November, and that there were disagreements over Flipkart's IPO plans and a liquidity event for leadership and employees; the paper said the decision was finalised after a breakdown in talks. Inc42, also citing sources, reported that Walmart's leadership asked Krishnamurthy to step down.

The IPO itself is deferred, with no new timeline. Flipkart had been targeting filing draft papers with SEBI by late 2026 or early 2027, The Economic Times reported, and it moved its registered headquarters from Singapore to India earlier in 2026 as part of its listing preparations. Bloomberg reported that Flipkart's valuation crossed $38 billion this year. Nicholas said Walmart did not need an IPO for cash and was prioritising long-term growth over the timing of a listing.

"To build this to be something that is around for the very long term is way more important than the timing of the IPO."

— Chris Nicholas, CEO, Walmart International, as reported by Bloomberg

The delay has had internal costs. The Economic Times reported that several vice presidents and senior executives left over the previous six to eight months over the delayed liquidity event, as current and former employees sought a buyback of stock options held for years; Inc42 put the number of senior-level departures over the past year at 14. Bloomberg reported that Walmart is developing a plan to provide liquidity to employees, without saying whether it would buy out former executives' options.

The tenure that ends

Krishnamurthy rejoined Flipkart in 2016 from Tiger Global, an early Flipkart investor, after an earlier stint as the company's chief finance officer and seven years in eBay's Asia finance operations. He led Flipkart through the Walmart acquisition after co-founders Sachin Bansal and Binny Bansal exited, and through its expansion against Amazon and Meesho. On quick commerce, Mint reported, he was initially hesitant about the cash-intensive business, but Flipkart launched Flipkart Minutes in 2024, ahead of Amazon's entry into instant delivery in India.

No next role for Krishnamurthy has been reported. What to watch is the successor announcement in the coming weeks — and whether Walmart pairs it with any new word on the IPO timetable or the employee liquidity plan.
